audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] gives Sett Levels 3 and 6 and calls First item 'Skill', but whys[2], whys[4] and whys[5] in the same object say Aatrox out-brawls him at 3, out-sustains the R combo at 6, and takes the extended brawl firmly at first item. The packet chart also reads Sett, Skill, then Aatrox through First item.
audit.why: Sett's damage is grit-gated and Facebreaker is 16s at rank 1 while The Darkin Blade is 10s at rank 3 and Umbral Dash 7s — Aatrox re-arms twice per Sett window once his kit is complete. 53.29% over 3817 games supports the shift.
audit.corrected: Level 2 evens to Skill; Levels 3 through First item belong to Aatrox; Two+ items stays Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes describe Haymaker and The Show Stopper without a single cooldown, so 'bait out his W' has no clock.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, The Show Stopper 120/100/80. Those numbers turn 'trade when his grit bar is empty' into a countable window.
audit.corrected: Haymaker's 18s rank-1 cooldown and Facebreaker's 16s added to the Lvl 3-5 and Lvl 6 spikes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two interactions that decide every Sett trade are absent. Haymaker deals true damage only in the centre of the punch and physical damage on the sides. Facebreaker stuns only when it pulls enemies from both sides of Sett; catch it with nothing opposite you and it is a slow instead.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides' and 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Standing off the centre line of Haymaker converts his best damage into something your armour and drain actually answer, and it is the one thing Aatrox can control mid-cast with Umbral Dash.
audit.corrected: Off-centre positioning against Haymaker and the both-sides condition on the Facebreaker stun now stated in spikes[0], spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[1].

audit.why: Trade advice was already right in shape — extend past his burst, drain grinds him out — it only lacked the mechanical reason.

edits.before: Your window opens — with full Q pattern + W you out-brawl Sett before his true damage scales. W-pull him, land Q sweetspots, and E-drain. Bait out his W (Haymaker) — the punch that shields and deals grit-based true damage — by trading when his grit bar is empty, then commit.
edits.after: Your window opens — with full Q pattern + W you out-brawl Sett before his true damage scales. Chain him, land Q sweetspots, E-drain. Haymaker (18s) only deals true damage down its centre — Umbral Dash sideways as he winds up and you eat the physical edge instead.

edits.before: His R (The Show Stopper) is a suppression lock-down that pairs with his E (Facebreaker) stun for a burst combo. Hold E to dodge his E pull-and-stun, save R to out-sustain his burst, and drain back the true damage he lands.
edits.after: The Show Stopper (120s) pairs with Facebreaker (16s) for the burst combo, but Facebreaker only stuns when it pulls enemies from both sides of him — fight with nothing behind him and it is a slow you drain straight through.

edits.before: From level 3 you take over — your full Q pattern and W pull out-brawl Sett before his true damage scales up. Pull him in, land Q sweetspots, and E-drain, but time it to his grit bar: trade when it's empty so his Haymaker shield-punch is weak, then commit through the drain. At 6 respect the E-stun into R suppression combo; hold E to dodge his Facebreaker and save R to out-sustain the burst. Your relentless damage beats his cooldown-gated punches.
edits.after: From level 3 you take over — your full Q pattern and Infernal Chains out-brawl Sett before his true damage scales. Chain him in, land Q sweetspots, E-drain, timed to his grit bar: trade when it is empty so the 18s Haymaker is weak, and step off its centre line, where the true damage lives, into the physical edge. At 6 respect Facebreaker into The Show Stopper; it only stuns if it catches enemies both sides of him.

edits.before: Land E stun into W Haymaker for burst trades
edits.after: Pull you into the true-damage centre of Haymaker

edits.before: Sett changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Sett E and W Haymaker. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Sett wants to force long trades, punish overextension, and turn one bad Aatrox cooldown into a lane-losing fight.
edits.after: Sett changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Facebreaker (E, 16s) into Haymaker, whose true damage lands only down the centre of the punch. Aatrox wins by spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, standing off that centre line, and holding Umbral Dash for the pull rather than the chase. Sett wants long trades and one spent Aatrox cooldown to end the lane.

notes: Facebreaker's stun condition is stated exactly as Riot words it (enemies on both sides). Whether minions on the far side satisfy that condition is not in the kit text and I did not assert it either way — flagged as unverified.
